chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man — I come to him and speak to him with some of my speech, and he understands all of it; and among them is one whom I come to and speak to him with the full speech, and he receives all of my speech completely, then returns it back to me just as I had spoken to him; and among them is one whom I come to and speak to him, and he says, "Repeat it to me".'

So he said: 'O Ishaq! And do you not know why this is so?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'The one to whom you speak with part of your speech and he understands all of it — that is one whose seed was kneaded with his intellect. As for the one to whom you speak and he receives your speech completely then answers you based on your speech — that is the one in whom his intellect was superimposed in the womb of his mother. And as for the one to whom you speak with the speech and he says, "Repeat it to me" — that is the one in whom his intellect was superimposed after he had grown old, so he says to you, "Repeat it to me".'

key_terms.رُكِّبَ: Superimposed/installed — a technical term indicating the divine act of integrating reason into the human person at different stages
key_terms.عَقْل: Intellect/reason (aql) — in Shia tradition, a divine faculty that enables comprehension of religious truths; its perfection varies among individuals
key_terms.عُجِنَتْ: Kneaded/mixed — describing the intimate union of intellect with the original seed, indicating the deepest pre-natal endowment of aql
key_terms.نُطْفَة: Nutfa — the initial seed/sperm from which a human develops; its kneading with aql signifies the highest intellectual endowment

ai.seo_question: Why do people differ in their ability to comprehend speech according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about three types of people who differ in how they comprehend speech: one who grasps the full meaning from partial speech, one who needs complete speech to respond accurately, and one who asks for repetition. The Imam explained that this variation in comprehension is due to when the aql (intellect/reason) was instilled in the person — before birth (mixed with the nutfa/seed), in the womb, or after maturity. This hadith reflects the Shia theological understanding of aql as a divinely bestowed faculty whose degree is determined before birth, providing a metaphysical basis for differences in human intellectual capacity.
